help: The Pip-Boy light on your head, in your hands or on your weapon: its beams, and the gestures that move it.

content.text: A VR replacement for the Pip-Boy flashlight that you handle like a real one: grab it off your belt, hold it in either hand, bring it to your head, or mount it on your weapon. Put it back on your belt to turn it off. Each place has its own beam, and changes apply live.

content.help: Opens the Immersive Flashlight wiki in your browser. Take off the headset to read it on your monitor.

content.text: <font color='#10FA78'>Flashlight positions:</font> Your flashlight can be in either hand, on your weapon, or on your head (with or without Power Armor). Its location is remembered separately inside and outside Power Armor.
<font color='#10FA78'>How to interact:</font> Move your hand near a flashlight interaction point. You'll feel a brief haptic tick when you're in range. Tap the trigger to interact.
<font color='#10FA78'>Belt flashlight:</font> Reach for the flashlight on your belt and tap the trigger to take it into your hand. Return it to your belt to turn it off.
<font color='#10FA78'>Head flashlight:</font> Bring your offhand near your head and tap the trigger to activate the head-mounted light directly, without first taking it into your hand.

<font color='#10FA78'>Transfer the light:</font> Bring your offhand near your primary hand and tap the trigger to move the light between hands or onto your weapon. Where it moves depends on its current position and whether you're holding a weapon.

<font color='#10FA78'>Automatic switching:</font> A light in your primary hand moves onto your gun when drawn, and turns off for melee weapons. A light in your offhand moves onto the gun when gripping it two-handed.
<font color='#10FA78'>Beam settings:</font> Each flashlight position has its own beam settings. Customize them independently on the Beam page.

<font color='#10FA78'>Requirements:</font> By default, mounting the light on your head requires a helmet or hard hat. Some weapon mods require a visible flashlight attachment to mount the light on a gun. Both restrictions can be changed on the General page.
<font color='#10FA78'>Enemy awareness:</font> Hostile NPCs may investigate when caught in your beam or near an area it illuminates. Configure this behavior on the Advanced page.

pages.help: Where the light is, its shadows, and what the flashlight needs.

content.help: Where the light is out of power armor. Moving it with your hands sets it too.
Where the light is in power armor, kept apart from the one out of it. On the head it is the helmet's lamp.
Whether the beam casts shadows. Shadows cost some performance.

content.text: <font color='#FFBF33'>WARNING: The game's Shadow Quality is below High</font>, which may break the beam's shadows. Set it to HIGH in the game's Settings > Performance, or turn flashlight shadows off.

content.help: Shows a warning when VR FPS Stabilizer is installed, as it lowers the game's shadow quality while you play, which breaks the beam's shadows.

content.text: <font color='#FFBF33'>WARNING: VR FPS Stabilizer is installed</font> - it lowers the game's shadow quality while you play, which may break the beam's shadows. Turn flashlight shadows off, or remove it.
Keep light on when opening Pip-Boy
content.help: Keeps the light on while the Pip-Boy is open. When off, the light goes off while the Pip-Boy is open, as in the base game.
Turns off the game's own flashlight toggle (offhand trigger long-press), so only this mod's gestures turn the light on and off.
A flashlight hangs on your belt while it isn't in your hand: reach for it to take the light, or put it back to turn it off. Off, there is no model and no grab.

content.text: Require headgear for flashlight on head
content.help: What you need on your head for the light to go there, out of power armor. Without it the head light is not allowed.

options.help: The light can always go on the head.
Helmets and hard hats, not soft hats.

content.text: Require a flashlight on the weapon
content.help: Whether the light goes on a weapon only when the weapon has a flashlight model. Without one the light on weapon is not allowed.

options.help: The light can always go on the weapon.
Only a weapon with a flashlight model.
Only a weapon with a flashlight model, while VRCP DOOM Merged or Tactical Weapon Mods is installed.

content.text: Supported weapon flashlight mod detected: VRCP DOOM Merged.
Supported weapon flashlight mod detected: Tactical Weapon Mods.
No supported weapon flashlight mod detected. "Not required" and "Required with a weapon mod" let the light go on any weapon, and "Required" keeps it off every weapon without a flashlight model.
Move the light when its place isn't allowed
content.help: When a requirement rules out where the light is, it moves to the next free place: your head, a free hand, then the weapon, and returns once its place is allowed again. When off, the light turns off instead.
Enemies your beam reaches, or who see where it lands, notice the light and come looking for its source. Fine-tune it on the Advanced page.

Reach a hand to the flashlight on your belt to take the light into that hand, or to put it back.
Bring the offhand to your head to put the light there, or to turn it off. Its zone is right in front of your eyes, so it shows no icons or sphere.
